question:
A 25-year-old woman presents to the clinic with complaints of dysuria and increased urinary frequency. Her urinalysis results are negative for nitrites. Urine microscopy shows the findings in figure A.

What is the most likely cause underlying her symptoms?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Dysuria and increased urinary frequency" -> "Negative nitrites on urinalysis" -> "Urine microscopy findings in figure A" -> "S. saprophyticus infection" -> 80% CHAIN: "Dysuria and increased urinary frequency" -> "Negative nitrites on urinalysis" -> "Urine microscopy findings in figure A" -> "Enterococci infection" -> 80%
analysis: The presence of white blood cells (WBCs) in the urine microscopy without nitrites in the urinalysis suggests a non-E. coli bacterial infection. S. saprophyticus is a common cause of urinary tract infections in young women, especially those who are sexually active. It is known to cause dysuria and increased urinary frequency.
